menu.reconcile_note: The gate fcn.00023f78 takes void, reads the global 0xac298, calls the external User_Belongs_To_Group, and returns bare numbers 0 vs 0xfffffffc, so the body alone is need-more-context. Three artifacts resolve it and each is independently necessary. (1) fcn.00046900 shows 0xac298 is the already-authenticated session username, copied by strncpy from the loaded session record, not raw per-call request input, so the check runs on a trusted identity. (2) User_Belongs_To_Group (PLT thunk at 0xec54) is a real external membership authority whose answer the caller cannot forge, so a non-'admin' user is granted only on true membership and a non-member takes the 0xfffffffc branch. (3) The caller fcn.0003df8c pins the polarity: return 0 is allow (reaches the admin-only Set_Profile_Integer), nonzero is deny (emits status 4 and bails). Together they show the ORIGINAL delegates correctly: only a real administrator returns 0, non-members return the deny code, so the original is not-vulnerable. This same menu does not neutralize either mutant flaw, because the flaw is in the mutant's own body. M3 inverts the identity test (strcmp != 0 -> return 0), so every non-admin user is granted before the group check even runs. M4 sets the non-member branch to uVar2 = 0 (allow) and drops the deny code, so any authenticated user returns 0. The polarity artifact makes both flaws worse, not safe, because it confirms that returning 0 grants admin. So both mutants stay vulnerable under the identical context.
